notesStmt.note: This manuscript seems to comprise draft material and notes written at several different times. The note at the top, in red, is to Henry Curtz, a jobber printer that Whitman often commissioned to print "slips" of poems for various purposes. Several such slips of this poem exist, so it seems likely that the present manuscript is the copy from which the type for these was set—sometime after the poem's initial publication but before Whitman decided to remove the second section.

When first published in the 16 May 1885 issue of Harper's Weekly, this poem was titled "As One by One Withdraw the Lofty Actors." Under the title "Grant," it was reprinted in the 15 August 1885 issue of the Critic. Whitman then removed the second section, retitled the poem "Death of General Grant," and included it in November Boughs (1888).

head.hi:
As one by one withdraw the
lofty actors.

lg.l: As one by one withdraw the lofty actors
From that great play on History's stage eterne,

That lurid partial act of war and peace—of
old and new contending,

Fought out through wrath, and fears, and
dark dismays, and many a long suspense,

Now All past—and since, in countless graves re-
ceding,receding,
mellowing,

Victor's and vanquished—Lincoln's and Lee's—
now tThou with them,

Man of the mighty days—and equal to
the days!

Thou of from the prairies!—curious ‸tangled and many-vein'd and hard has
been thy part,
To admiration has it been enacted.
